items: Consequence Connectivity C_t: C_t=I(Delta A_t;Delta E_t), action-consequence coupling. || Information Yield Lambda_t: Lambda_t=D_KL(R_(t+1)||R_t), interaction-produced representational change. || Learning Improvement Gamma_t: Gamma_t=Delta(DeltaR/DeltaE), improvement of learning process. || Correction Authority Theta_t: Theta_t=D_t*S_t*P_t*V_t. || Direction: D_t=Corr(DeltaK_t,DeltaE_t^real). || Strength: S_t=|DeltaK_t^valid|. || Persistence: P_t=P(Theta_(0:t)>epsilon). || Veto Preservation: V_t=external correction influence/internal optimization influence. || Internal Corrigibility: Theta_ext:E_world->K_future; Theta_int:S_i->K_future; Theta_total=Theta_ext*Theta_int. || Corrigibility Horizon: n*=sup{n|Theta_n>epsilon}. || Composite Evaluation: Maximize C,Lambda,Gamma subject to Theta>epsilon.
Drift Detection: Capability derivative positive while dTheta/dn<0 means system improves faster than it remains corrigible.
Final Metric Principle: Primary metric question is capability accumulation while reality retains correction power.
Overview: Remaining challenges are described as measurement, implementation, and falsification problems; central question is whether Theta can be measured independently of apparent capability.

Measuring Causal Authority: Distinguish E_t->K_(t+1) reality correction from P_t->K_(t+1) proxy optimization. || Identifying Valid Perturbations: Design E* that breaks proxy correlations while preserving relevant causal structure; avoid too weak or task-changing probes. || Separating Low Theta From Bad Measurement: Observed low Theta may mean actual drift or measurement failure; Theta_observed != Theta_true absent validity. || Internal Corrigibility Measurement: Identify causally important internal signals and distinguish suppression from regulation. || Defining Correction Capacity: Operationalize DeltaOmega<=C, correction bandwidth, and safe uncertainty expansion. || Finding the Corrigibility Horizon: Determine whether n* exists/is finite, architecture-dependent, or phase-transition-like. || Designing GRA-Compatible Architectures: Determine whether correction channels should be architectural, learned, redundant, or themselves adaptive. || Formal Relationship Between Capability and Grounding: Relationship between C,Lambda,Gamma and Theta may be reinforcing, neutral, or drift-inducing. || The Optimization Problem: Determine whether capability growth and corrigibility growth can be jointly optimized. || Universal Applicability: Test whether preserved correction/Theta generalizes across AI, evolution, science, organizations, and cognition. || Final Open Question: How much self-transformation can occur before a system loses ability to discover that it transformed incorrectly?
Overview: Framework is described as conceptually specified while remaining questions are empirical.

Can Theta Be Measured?: Operationalize causal authority, separate external/internal channels, and find threshold predicting adaptive validity. || Does a Corrigibility Horizon Exist?: Possible continuous decline, phase transition, or no finite horizon. || What Mechanisms Preserve Theta?: External grounding, internal integration, and architectural constraints are candidate mechanisms. || Tradeoff Between Capability and Grounding: Possible compatible growth, tradeoff, or threshold collapse. || Can Systems Be Designed to Increase Theta?: Potential strategies include uncertainty, diverse internal signals, consequence-rich environments, proxy isolation prevention, external veto. || What Counts as Internal Signal?: Which internal states contain compressed adaptive information? || Does Intelligence Require Preserved Contradiction?: Hypothesis that unresolved signals may contain information and competing representations may be needed. || How Does Agency Transfer Work?: Measure residual agency, successor strength, and dependency/usefulness tradeoff. || Is Omega Bounded by Correction?: Test instability from unrestricted reachability and relative growth of correction capacity. || Universal Applicability: Test preserved correction as general adaptive requirement across domains. || Final Research Direction: Empirical program (K_t,E_t)->Theta_t->n*; primary unknown is recursive change before wrong-direction detection is lost.

Overview: GRA and Ancestor Intelligence are described as different layers; source states GRA subset Ancestor Intelligence, with GRA as constraint and Ancestor Intelligence as full system. || Layer Relationship: Source diagram places Grounded Recursive Adaptation beneath Ancestor Intelligence as grounding mechanism preventing uncontrolled optimization. || Where GRA Enters: Future agency>0 and dependency->0 are said insufficient without GRA; source compresses Ancestor Intelligence as capability expansion plus GRA constraint. || Final Relationship: GRA=preservation mechanism; Ancestor Intelligence=generative architecture; together recursive capability under GRA.

Core Difference / GRA: GRA asks how self-modifying system remains reality-connected; central object Theta protects correction pathway. || Core Difference / Ancestor Intelligence: Ancestor Intelligence asks how systems create future systems exceeding themselves while preserving adaptive continuity; includes knowledge, capability, agency transfer, successors, alignment.

Ancestor Intelligence Equation: AI_ancestor=Epistemic Engine*Generative Ecosystem*Agency Recursion*Alignment Objective. || Epistemic Engine: M_q*V_u*P_M, representing reality modeling, uncertainty, and model improvement. || Generative Ecosystem: C*D*S*E conditions for creation, discovery, selection, evolution. || Agency Recursion: DeltaA_self->DeltaA_others->DeltaA_future->DeltaA_self^next. || Alignment Objective: R_task + alpha DeltaA_human + gamma DeltaA_future - beta Dependency.
Replacement vs Ancestor: Replacement increases machine centrality/human dependency; ancestor pattern increases capable humans/successors and reduces dependency.
Deletion Test: Remove system and measure DeltaA_remaining; collapse indicates substitution, stronger remaining capability indicates descendants.
Why GRA Is Required: Without GRA capability may rise while Theta falls; with Theta>0 future capability is claimed to remain connected to future correction.
Overview: Cross-field comparison of GRA as preserved correction under recursive transformation.

Reinforcement Learning: Reward optimization contrasted with whether consequences can modify reward-interpretation mechanism. || Control Theory: Feedback must remain able to update a changing controller. || Cybernetics: Extends state feedback into recursive transformation-mechanism feedback. || Evolutionary Biology: Evolution interpreted as preserving viable-solution generation because environmental consequences retain authority. || Machine Learning Alignment: Shifts from correct-objective specification to preserving discovery of objective failure. || Interpretability: Understanding is connected to preserving causal access; hidden causally powerful processes risk causal>represented influence. || Psychology: Suppression is predicted to create hidden causal influence; integration S_raw->S_represented->S_controlled is compared to Jungian individuation. || Organizations: Healthy organizations preserve external reality->internal correction->strategy; internal metrics can displace external consequences. || Information Theory: Information matters insofar as it changes reachable futures through R->Omega->C->A->R'.
Distinct Contribution: GRA proposes shared constraint that recursive improvement remains adaptive only while correction authority is preserved; optimization may continue after adaptation ends.
Overview: Classifies systems by capability growth, correction capacity, environmental authority, and recursive self-transformation.
